claim: Calorie deficit required for fat loss; surplus for gain
note: First law; all diets equal at matched calories (Hall Lancet 2011).
Adaptive thermogenesis is real but modest (Martins Br J Nutr 2022) — not a hard 'starvation mode'. Reverse-diet 100-150 kcal/week protocol is heuristic, not RCT-proven.
cite: Martins et al. Br J Nutr 2022

claim: Protein 1.6-2.2 g/kg preserves muscle on cut
note: ISSN position stand: 1.4-2.0 total, 2.3-3.1 g/kg FFM when dieting.

claim: Creatine monohydrate is well-researched, intracellular water
note: CP->ATP; not subcutaneous bloat (ISSN creatine stand).
Whey > BCAA for MPS (Jackman 2017; Morton 2018 meta).

claim: LISS raises cortisol -> eats muscle; HIIT spares muscle
note: Both raise cortisol acutely (HIIT often more). Muscle loss = deficit + no lifting + low protein, not cardio type (Tremblay 1994 mis-cited).

claim: Drinking more water directly burns fat
note: Small transient thermogenesis only (~20-100 kcal). Hydration helps function, not fat oxidation.
Only fixes deficiency; no effect in replete (Wilborn 2004, Koehler 2009).
Essential in theory, no glycemic benefit in non-diabetics.
No superior fat loss at isocaloric (Bueno Br J Nutr 2013, Cochrane CD013334).

claim: Refeed boosts leptin and accelerates loss
note: Refeeds raise leptin acutely (Dirlewanger Int J Obes 2000) but metabolic advantage is weak; mainly adherence.
